XXIIII.}}</noinclude>vvhom also being apprehended vve vvould haue iudged according to our lavv. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=7}}† But Lysias the Tribune comming in, vvith great force tooke him avvay out of our handes, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=8}}† commaunding his accusers to come to thee, of vvhom thou maiest thy self iudging, vnderstand of al these things, vvhereof vve accuse him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=9}}† And the Ievves also added, saying that these things vvere so. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=10}}† But Paul ansvvered, (the President making a signe vnto him for to speake.) Knovving that of many yeres thou art iudge ouer this nation, I vvil vvith good courage ansvver for my self. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=11}}† For thou maiest vnderstand that it is not aboue tvvelue daies to me, since I vvent vp to adore in Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=12}}† and neither in the temple did they finde me disputing vvith any man, or causing concourse of the multitude, neither in the synagogs, nor in the citie: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=13}}† neither can they proue vnto thee the things vvhereof they novv accuse me. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=14}}† But this I confesse to thee, that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν''}}∷ according to the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Because Tertullus the Ievves orator called Christian religion the sect or (as it is there vers.5 in the Greeke) the heresie of the Nazarens: S. Paul ansvvereth and shevveth that it is no heresie. And as for the vvord, ''Sect'', in this place: it is in the Greeke, ''According to the vvay, vvhich they call heresie'', as also Act. 9, 2. 24, 22. And therfore the vvord sect here is so taken. See ''Annot. c. 28, 22''.}}∷ secte, vvhich they call heresie, I doe so serue {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`the God of my fathers'',}}`the father my God', beleeuing al things that are vvritten in the Law & the Prophets: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=15}}† hauing hope in God, the vvhich these also them selues expect, that there shal be a resurrection of iust and vniust. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=16}}† In this my self also doe studie to haue a cōscience vvithout offense tovvard God & tovvard men alvvaies. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=17}}† And after many yeres {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ro. 15, 28.''}}* I came to bestovv almes vpon my nation, & oblations, and vovves. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=18}}† In the vvhich they found me {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 21, 26.''}}* purified in the temple: not vvith multitude nor vvith tumult. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=19}}† But certaine Ievves of Asia, vvho ought to be present before thee and to accuse, if they had any thing against me: {{verse|chapter=24|verse=20}}† or let these men thē selues say, if they haue found in me any iniquitie, forasmuch as I stand in the Councel, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=21}}† but of this one voice only that I cried standing among them, That {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 23, 6.''}}* of the resurrection of the dead am I iudged this day of you. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=22}}† And Felix differred them, knovving most certainely of this vvay, saying, Vvhen Lysias the Tribune is come dovvne, I vvil heare you. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=23}}† And he commaunded the Centurion to keepe him, and that he should haue rest, neither to prohibit any of his to minister vnto him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=24}}† And after some daies, Felix comming vvith Drusilla his vvife, vvhich vvas a Ievve, called Paul, and heard of him the faith that is in Christ {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=25}}† And he disputing of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Apostolike teaching vvas not of only or special faith, but of iustice, & chastitie, & iudgement, that is to say, of the terrour of Hel and other Gods iudgements in the next life ansvverable to our deedes in this vvorld: by vvhich the hearers vvere first terrified, and so induced to penance. Hovv say Heretikes then that such things make men hypocrites?}}∷ iustice and chastitie, and of the iudgement to come, Felix<noinclude>{{rh|||being}}</noinclude>
